title: yupana: code-fact freshness tracked but unserved; CLAUDE.md claim incomplete
description: yupana watch/overlay_refresh.rs maintains real Recomputing-to-Fresh transitions but freshness_handle/freshness_of have zero production callers outside the module; no query surface serves code-fact freshness (correctly omitted, per FR-3). CLAUDE.md's 'freshness half is Phase 3, not yet served' is incomplete: the verdict surface serves PROJECTION freshness (src/hook/rule_planes.rs:546-566, src/verdict.rs:129). Distinguish code-fact vs projection freshness in docs; wire tracked freshness into query responses at Phase 3.
notes: PARTIALLY VERIFIED 2026-08-17 (Claude) — deliberately NOT closed, unlike the other six yupana beads re-verified this pass. This bead has two asks and they are in different states. DONE: 'distinguish code-fact vs projection freshness in docs'. yupana CLAUDE.md now says it explicitly — FR-3's freshness half splits in two, code-fact freshness is tracked by src/watch/overlay_refresh.rs but not served, while the verdict surface already serves PROJECTION freshness (src/hook/rule_planes.rs, src/verdict.rs), and 'don't mistake one for the other'. That was the bead's actionable-now half and it is resolved. NOT DONE: 'wire tracked freshness into query responses at Phase 3'. freshness_of has gained a production caller (src/daemon/mod.rs:130, tested at src/daemon/http_test.rs:491-521) so it is reachable, but a query response still omits the tag rather than faking 'fresh' — which yupana's CLAUDE.md states is the correct behaviour until Phase 3 wires it through. So this stays open: the remaining clause is scheduled, not overdue, and closing it would delete the only tracker entry for Phase 3 serving work. Whoever starts Phase 3 should either finish this or split the remainder into its own bead.

Provisional D section 9.2(3) (camayoc docs/patents/provisional-grounding-cluster.md) discloses the combined pre-landing gate as contemplated — implement verify as an opt-in arm of pre-edit within its latency budget.

title: paper: establish which ablation arms are valid — measurements predate two bug fixes
description: The context-injection paper draft (docs/paper-context-injection.md) is dated 2026-03-05. Two bugs in mechanisms it ablates were fixed 2026-08-17, five months later: cee3cdc (complementary expansion kept non-adjacent duplicates, so one file could consume several of the five truncated slots) and 7d99f03 (intent doc-demotion factor inverted on the local hook path — a 1.5 factor that strengthened demotion remotely weakened it locally). The 66-run and 85-run measurements were therefore taken against code where at least two mechanisms did not behave as the paper describes them. Determine per-arm which numbers survive. Complementary expansion and coupling expansion are distinct mechanisms, so the reported -0.247 coupling arm may be unaffected; that needs checking rather than assuming. Outcome is either a re-run of the affected arms or an explicit statement that all numbers are against a pinned pre-fix commit, with the divergence named. Do not draft around these numbers until this is settled.
acceptance_criteria: Each reported figure is either re-measured post-fix, or attributed to a named commit with the behavioural divergence stated in the paper.

title: paper: lead with the ablation, not the aggregate improvement
description: The draft's headline is F1 0.695 -> 0.722 and duration 252s -> 209s. That is +0.027 F1 across 66 runs and it will not survive review as a primary claim; a reviewer asks for significance and gets an uncomfortable answer. The strong result is the decomposition, where the effects are large and unambiguous: semantic search -0.384 when disabled, git blame bridging -0.303, temporal coupling expansion -0.247. Restructure so the contribution is 'which of six injection methods actually carries the weight, measured by removal' rather than 'injection helps'. The aggregate improvement becomes a supporting number, not the thesis. This is the same editorial move that fixed the yupana paper plan: the decomposition is the result, the margin is not.
acceptance_criteria: Abstract and introduction lead with the ablation decomposition; the aggregate delta appears as support, not as the headline.

title: paper: significance testing and power for the thin ablation conditions
description: The draft's own abstract concedes 'small sample sizes for several ablation conditions'. Conceding it is not the same as quantifying it. Add confidence intervals or appropriate tests to every reported ablation effect, and name explicitly which conditions are underpowered rather than leaving the reader to infer it from run counts. If an arm cannot support a claim, say so and drop the claim — an ablation table with three solid rows and an honest gap is stronger than six rows of which half are noise. Pairs with the reframe bead: if the ablation is the thesis, its statistics carry the paper.
acceptance_criteria: Every ablation effect reports an interval or test; underpowered conditions are named in the results section, not only in the discussion.

title: paper: write the related work section — none exists
description: The draft has no related work at all. Areas to cover: retrieval-augmented generation and hybrid lexical+dense retrieval; rank fusion (RRF is the baseline a reviewer names by default); code search; agent context management and context-window budgeting; repository-history supervision (using commit history as labels is the paper's most unusual move and needs positioning against whatever exists); and Monitor-Guided Decoding, which is the nearest neighbour to injecting analysis facts into a model's loop. Reuse the bibliography assembled for the quipu paper where it overlaps rather than rebuilding it.
acceptance_criteria: A related work section positioning both headline mechanisms — blame-provenance bridging and commit-history-supervised calibration — against named prior work.

title: paper: move the small-N limitation into the abstract
description: Sample-size limits currently live in the discussion. With 66 runs across 13 tasks and several thin ablation arms, that belongs in the abstract. Stating a limit early is a credibility asset and costs nothing; discovering it late reads as concealment. Same discipline the yupana eval note already follows with its explicit threats-to-validity section.
acceptance_criteria: The abstract states the run counts and the small-sample caveat.

title: paper: arXiv submission mechanics for the bobbin paper
description: Follow the process already proven on the quipu submission (arXiv:submit/7961151, filed 2026-08-17): categories, licence, build verification against the local artifact, and the External DOI trap. Likely cs.SE primary with cs.AI cross-list, the reverse of quipu's. Endorsement is already held for cs.AI. The draft is markdown and will need a LaTeX conversion; quipu/docs/paper/ is the working template.
acceptance_criteria: Submitted, with the announcement mail received — moderation can still return category or technical issues, so submission alone is not done.

title: yupana: exemplar extraction for policy-by-example — spool ref to selector + tiered predicate candidates
description: quipu docs/design/policy-by-example.md, sequencing step 2. Given a verdict-spool reference (or commit+path+hunk), extract the structural context of the offending text as an aegis:Selector (yupana already knows the node: line_comment, string, identifier, import, file class) and emit predicate candidates at each viable tier: the exact token/id for membership, a generated narrowing pattern offered for human approval, and the exemplar's embedding as a similarity anchor with a threshold suggested from quipu's backtest. Output feeds quipu-6bl's drafting scaffold; the placement check remains the refusal authority.
close_reason: VERIFIED IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-17 (Claude). yupana src/exemplar.rs exists and its header cites this bead and quipu docs/design/policy-by-example.md sequencing step 2; the machine feed is wired at src/cli_analyze.rs:349, whose comment states the output is a feed for quipu's drafting scaffold -- exactly the handoff the bead specified.

title: Failure and post-tool-use injections lack injection IDs and bypass the session ledger
description: Only prompt-submission paths generate injection identifiers and store injection records (src/cli/hook.rs:1450/1509, 3219/3234-3246); the failure-handler's semantic fallback passes None (hook.rs:4672) and the parse-directed and post-tool-use paths store nothing, so those injections cannot be rated via feedback. They neither filter against nor record to the SessionLedger (hook.rs:1164-1176/1481, 3089-3110/3274-3276), so they can re-inject chunks the prompt path already delivered, invisible to delta filtering. Extend the ID scheme and ledger integration to all injecting event classes. Found by adversarial doc-vs-code review (Claude agent session, 2026-08-14).

title: file-size ratchet red on main: 10 files over the 500-line limit
description: just check fails on main before any change is made: scripts/check-file-size.sh reports 10 errors (src/cli/bead.rs 1179 lines, src/http/handlers/archive.rs 846, src/cli/ontology.rs 663, src/index/cross_repo.rs 620, six more) and 7 warnings. A permanently-red gate trains contributors to ignore it — the control-that-cannot-fail failure mode. Pitch: split the ten files or move them deliberately to scripts/large-file-allowlist.txt with rationale, restoring the gate's meaning.
notes: SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-17 (Claude): this bead says 10 files over the 500-line limit and names src/cli/bead.rs (1,179) as the worst. Measured: 42 files, headed by src/cli/hook.rs at 8,050 -- sixteen times the limit and nearly seven times the largest file this bead mentions. Command: find src -name '*.rs' -exec wc -l {} + | awk '$1>500 && $2!="total"' | wc -l. That changes the WORK, not just the priority: 'split the ten files or allowlist them' is a different job against 42 led by an 8,050-line one, and anyone scoping from this bead sizes it wrong by an order of magnitude. Re-scope before dispatch. Detail in docs/plans/bobbin-debt.md section 1. Not actioned -- splitting these is the large change the ranger charter reserves for polecats.

title: Complementary expansion dedup misses non-adjacent duplicates
description: src/cli/hook.rs:3158-3159 sorts complementary candidates by coupling score descending, then dedup_by(|a,b| a.0 == b.0), which removes only consecutive equal-path entries. A file reached via multiple seen files with different scores survives as duplicates and can consume several of the 5 truncated slots. Dedupe by path (keep max score per path) before sorting/truncating. Found by adversarial doc-vs-code review (Claude agent session, 2026-08-14).
close_reason: Fixed: extracted dedupe_complementary (max score per path, sorted, truncated). dedup_by removes only CONSECUTIVE equal entries and the sort was by score not path, so duplicates were adjacent only by coincidence and ate the 5 slots. Ties break by path -- HashMap order varies per run and would otherwise make injected context differ between identical invocations. The extraction is part of the fix: the old form was buried mid-function and untestable, which is why a dedup that deduped nothing went unnoticed. 5 tests, 928 passed. Commit cee3cdc.

title: bd/bobbin: duplicate work-item advisory at bead creation via beads-index similarity

title: yupana: denied-edit recurrence advisory — the verdict spool as a similarity corpus
description: quipu docs/design/semantic-grounded-edit-policies.md, Further applications #5. The verdict spool already retains refused-edit verdicts; embed them and, at the edit seam, surface the nearest prior denial as stage-1 advisory context ('a similar edit was denied under policy X') BEFORE the stage-2 policy evaluation that may refuse. The agent learns from refusals it never saw; similarity never denies — only the exact policy tier does. Score/threshold/model/corpus-watermark in the advisory; identify-and-inform-before-refusing ordering per the design doc.

title: Intent doc-demotion factor has opposite semantics in local vs remote hook paths
description: The remote path inverts into effect space before applying the intent factor (src/cli/hook.rs:1082-1090: effect=(1-dd)*factor; dd'=1-effect), so BugFix's 1.5 factor strengthens demotion as intended. The local path raw-multiplies the score multiplier (src/cli/hook.rs:2873: (base_dd * adj.doc_demotion_factor).clamp(0.01, 1.0)), so the same factor raises the multiplier and WEAKENS demotion — the opposite effect. The local path should adopt the effect-space form. Found by adversarial doc-vs-code review (Claude agent session, 2026-08-14).
close_reason: Fixed: both hook paths now call search::intent::apply_doc_demotion_factor. doc_demotion is a score MULTIPLIER, so lower = stronger demotion; the local path raw-multiplied and inverted every intent (BugFix/Operational surfaced MORE docs, Architecture FEWER) against the contract src/search/intent.rs's own tests assert. Fixed as a shared function rather than a corrected line, because the defect was two copies of one calculation disagreeing. 7 tests incl. one walking the whole intent table asserting the arithmetic matches each entry's comment. 928 passed, 0 failed; clippy unchanged at 207. Commit 7d99f03.

title: yupana: project the work-item grounding set into the hot plane; three-outcome entity-grounded evaluation
description: Consumes quipu-3aj's vocabulary (quipu docs/design/semantic-grounded-edit-policies.md). Project the authoritative work-item id set alongside the rules under the existing freshness/cache-age machinery; evaluate candidates by O(1) membership within the 5ms budget; report grounded / unresolvable (fabricated reference, its own violation class) / no-candidate; missing grounding projection renders the rule unevaluated (loud), never satisfied-by-empty-set. Bitemporal follow-on: todo-needs-ticket v2 requires the cited item open at edit time, computed at read.
notes: Rev 2: no regex anywhere. Exact tier = tokenize introduced text, hash-set membership per token. New embedding tier: project the work-item vector matrix (source: bobbin's own beads index, src/index/beads.rs) into the hot plane; brute-force cosine over a few thousand vectors; verdict carries score/threshold/model/corpus-watermark; advisory or escalate placement only.
close_reason: VERIFIED IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-17 (Claude). yupana src/project_grounding.rs cites this bead and the design doc; src/project.rs:215 and src/projection_cache.rs:78 carry the entity-grounded rules through the existing cache-age machinery. The requirement most likely to be silently dropped is explicitly honoured: src/project.rs:318 comments 'satisfied by an empty set (bobbin-tvn)' at the guard preventing exactly that. Embedding tier at src/grounding/similarity.rs.

title: Topic fingerprint truncates top-10 alphabetically, not by score
description: compute_session_id (src/cli/hook.rs:2273-2293) collects above-threshold chunk keys, sorts alphabetically, then truncates to 10 before hashing — so which chunks enter the fingerprint depends on path lexicography, not relevance. If intentional, document it; if not, sort by score, truncate, then sort keys for hash stability. Found by adversarial doc-vs-code review (Claude agent session, 2026-08-14).
notes: CONFIRMED + SPECIFIED, NOT APPLIED 2026-08-17 (Claude). Verified exactly as filed at src/cli/hook.rs: keys.sort() is lexicographic then truncate(10), and c.score is in scope one line above and discarded. Fix: sort_by(score desc), truncate, THEN keys.sort() again -- the re-sort must come AFTER the truncate so the hash depends on the selected SET and not on score order, otherwise the fingerprint churns whenever two scores swap without the set changing. f32 has no total order, so partial_cmp with a fallback, not sort_by_key. NOT applied: it changes session identity, so every existing fingerprint changes value and the SessionLedger's progressive-reduction state sees a discontinuity on upgrade. That needs a migration decision and a ledger test. Full spec in docs/plans/bobbin-debt.md section 3.
